{{Short description|FIFA World Cup group}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=December 2025}}
{{Use American English|date=July 2026}}
Group F of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] took place from June 14 to 25, 2026.<ref name="match schedule">{{cite web |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/1be9ce37eb98fcc5/original/FWC26-Match-Schedule_English.pdf |title=FIFA World Cup 26 – Match Schedule |publisher=[[FIFA]] |date=February 4, 2024 |access-date=February 4, 2024}}</ref> The group consisted of the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]], [[Japan national football team|Japan]], [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]], and [[Tunisia national football team|Tunisia]].

The Netherlands topped the group, winning two games and drawing the other. Japan finished as runners-up, winning one game and drawing the other two. Both teams advanced to the [[2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 32|round of 32]].

Sweden finished in third place, and their performance allowed them to advance as one of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-place teams|eight best third-place teams]].<ref name="regulations">{{cite web |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/636f5c9c6f29771f/original/FWC2026_regulations_EN.pdf |title=FIFA World Cup 2026 Regulations |publisher=FIFA |date=May 2025 |access-date=June 7, 2025 |archive-date=June 23, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250623212158/https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/636f5c9c6f29771f/original/FWC2026_regulations_EN.pdf |url-status=live}}</ref>

However, the three teams performed poorly in the round of 32 and were eliminated from the World Cup. Tunisia were eliminated after losing their first two group games, and would go on to lose their third.

==Standings==
{{2026 FIFA World Cup group tables|Group F}}

In the [[2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 32|round of 32]]:<ref name="regulations"/>
* The winner of Group F, the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]], advanced to play the runner-up of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group C|Group C]], [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]].
* The runner-up of Group F, [[Japan national football team|Japan]], advanced to play the winner of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group C|Group C]], [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]].
* The third-place team of Group F, [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]], advanced to play the winner of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group I|Group I]], [[France national football team|France]], as one of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-place teams|eight best third-place teams]] from the group stage.

==Matches==
All times listed are local.<ref name="match schedule"/>

===Netherlands vs Japan===
[[File:Netherlands v Japan (2026 FIFA World Cup - Group F).jpg|thumb|Pre-match ceremony between Netherlands and Japan]]
The teams had met three times prior, including the Netherlands' [[2010 FIFA World Cup Group E#Netherlands vs Japan|1–0 group stage victory]] at the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Netherlands vs. Japan Head-to-Head in the World Cups|url=https://www.thesoccerworldcups.com/head_to_head/holland_vs_japan.php|website=The Soccer World Cups|access-date=December 5, 2025}}</ref> Their most recent meeting took place in 2013, a 2–2 friendly draw.<ref>{{cite web|title=Netherlands national football team: record v Japan|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/netherlands/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Japan|website=11v11.com|access-date=December 5, 2025}}</ref>

Coincidentally, both teams finished with a 2–2 draw in their opening match, with [[Virgil van Dijk]] being named as Man of the Match.

===Sweden vs Tunisia===
The teams had met on four previous occasions, always in friendlies. Tunisia won the most recent meeting in 2003, by 1–0.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tunisia national football team: record v Sweden|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/tunisia/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Sweden/|website=11v11.com|access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref>

The fixture marked Sweden's return to a major tournament after [[UEFA Euro 2020 knockout stage#Sweden vs Ukraine|five years]], having failed to qualify for both the [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022 World Cup]] and [[UEFA Euro 2024]]. Additionally, Sweden's five goals were the second-most the team has ever scored in a single World Cup match, behind only their 8–0 victory over [[Cuba national football team|Cuba]] in [[1938 FIFA World Cup|1938]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=15 June 2026 |title=Why Tunisia made shocking decision to fire manager Sabri Lamouchi in middle of 2026 World Cup|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/sweden-smash-five-past-tunisia-world-cup-opener-2026-06-15/ |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>

After the match, Tunisia manager [[Sabri Lamouchi]] was relieved from his managing duties. It was the first time that a manager was sacked during the [[FIFA World Cup]] since the [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998]] edition when Tunisia’s then manager [[Henryk Kasperczak]] and his side lost its first two group stage matches 2–0 to [[England national football team|England]] and 1–0 to [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]] respectively.<ref>{{cite web|title=Why Tunisia made shocking decision to fire manager Sabri Lamouchi in middle of 2026 World Cup|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/why-tunisia-made-shocking-decision-140435324.html|last=Mader|first=Daniel|website=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|access-date=15 June 2026}}</ref> Additionally, [[Carlos Alberto Parreira]], who was managing [[Saudi Arabia national football team|Saudi Arabia]], and [[Cha Bum-kun]], who was managing [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]], both in the same tournament, were also terminated after their first two matches as well.

===Netherlands vs Sweden===
The teams had met on 25 previous occasions, including a scoreless draw during the [[1974 FIFA World Cup Group 3|group stage]] at the [[1974 FIFA World Cup]], and most recently in a 2–0 win for the Netherlands in a [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group A|World Cup Qualifier]] match in 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Head to head: Netherlands vs Sweden|url=https://inside.fifa.com/en/data-centre/head-to-head/men/netherlands-vs-sweden|website=fifa.com|access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref>

[[Brian Brobbey]] scored in the fifth and seventeenth minute, the fourth-fastest brace in World Cup history.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carr |first=Harry |date=2026-06-20 |title=Netherlands 5–1 Sweden Stats: Brobbey and Gakpo at the Double as Dutch Sweep Swedes Aside |url=https://theanalyst.com/articles/netherlands-vs-sweden-stats-world-cup-2026 |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=Opta Analyst |language=en}}</ref> The fixture was Sweden's worst defeat at the World Cup since [[1950 FIFA World Cup final round#Brazil vs Sweden|being thrashed 7–1 by Brazil in 1950]], which also remains Brazil's biggest win in a tournament match. The win set a new record for the longest unbeaten run in World Cup history, with fourteen matches (spanning from the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]] and excluding 2018, which they failed to qualify for), surpassing the previous record by Brazil.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kovbasa |first=Ivan |date=2026-06-20 |title=Netherlands set new record for longest unbeaten run in World Cup history |url=https://tribuna.com/en/news/2026-06-20-netherlands-set-new-record-for-longest-unbeaten-run-in-world-cup-history/ |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=Tribuna.com}}</ref>

<section begin="F3" />{{#invoke:football box|main

|team1={{#invoke:flag|fb-rt|NED}}

|team2={{#invoke:flag|fb|SWE}}

===Tunisia vs Japan===
The teams have previously met six times, including Japan's [[2002 FIFA World Cup Group H#Tunisia vs Japan|2–0 group stage victory]] at the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]] (which they co-hosted with South Korea). Their latest meeting took place in the 2023 Kirin Challenge Cup, which Japan also won by 2–0.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tunisia national football team: record v Japan|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/tunisia/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Japan|website=11v11.com|access-date=5 December 2025}}</ref>

This fixture was the 1,000th World Cup match, with the previous milestone (900th) having been reached in the [[2018 FIFA World Cup final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/47224100/fifa-2026-world-cup-match-schedule-final-kickoff-usa|title=2026 World Cup schedule: FIFA reveals match times, locations|work=ESPN|access-date=7 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Milestone matches at the FIFA World Cup |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/milestone-landmark-matches-first |website=www.fifa.com |access-date=27 May 2026}}</ref> Moments before kickoff, a special pre-game celebration ceremony was held at the stadium with [[Hisako, Princess Takamado|Princess Takamado]] (Honorary Patron of the [[Japan Football Association]]) in attendance.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 June 2026 |title=Match 1,000 host Monterrey bids farewell to FIFA World Cup 2026 after four memorable games |url=https://inside.fifa.com/organisation/news/monterrey-stadium-world-cup-2026-netherlands-morocco-almeyda |access-date=3 July 2026 |website=[[FIFA]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=22 June 2026 |title=Gianni Infantino, Princess Takamado celebrate FIFA World Cup Match 1,000 with sell-out crowd |url=https://inside.fifa.com/organisation/news/princess-takamodo-japan-world-cup-match-1000-ramos-stoichkov |access-date=3 July 2026 |website=[[FIFA]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Tan |first=Gabriel |date=21 June 2026 |title=In FIFA World Cup's milestone 1,000th match, Japan arise to make history of their own |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49132600/in-fifa-world-cup-milestone-1000th-match-japan-arise-make-history-their-own |access-date=3 July 2026 |work=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>

With Tunisia losing their match, they became the third team to be eliminated from the tournament, following [[Haiti national football team|Haiti]] and [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]], after losing two consecutive matches. Additionally, Tunisia became the sole African team to be eliminated from the group stage. 

As for Japan, they became the first [[Asian Football Confederation|Asian]] team to score multiple goals in a single FIFA World Cup match, surpassing their own previous scoring record set during a [[2010 FIFA World Cup Group E#Denmark vs Japan|3–1 victory]] over [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]] in [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010]].

===Japan vs Sweden===
The teams had met five times, with Japan's only win from the notorious match in the [[Football at the 1936 Summer Olympics|1936 Olympics]] in the first round. Their most recent meeting, a friendly in 2002, ended in a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite web|title=Japan national football team: record v Sweden|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/japan/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Sweden/|website=11v11.com|access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref>

In the 56th minute, Japan took the lead when [[Daizen Maeda]] scored with a low shot after running onto a pass from [[Ritsu Dōan]] in the penalty area. [[Anthony Elanga]] equalised in the 62nd minute when he curled into the net from out on the right edge of the penalty area, low into the left corner of the net. The draw was enough for Japan to finish in second place in the group.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c74ydkzdg7et|title= Japan 1 Sweden 1|date=25 June 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=26 June 2026}}</ref>

===Tunisia vs Netherlands===
[[File:Netherlands vs Tunisia - 2026 FIFA World Cup, Kansas City.jpg|thumb|Pre-match ceremony between Tunisia and the Netherlands]]

The teams had previously faced each other thrice, most recently in a 2009 friendly match that ended in a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tunisia national football team: record v Netherlands|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/tunisia/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Netherlands|website=11v11.com|access-date=5 December 2025}}</ref>

With Tunisia already eliminated, they were off to a very shaky start. [[Ellyes Skhiri]] committed a costly own goal in the third minute, which allowed the formidable Dutch team to stretch the lead. [[Brian Brobbey]] would follow with a shot four minutes later. On the second half, Tunisia's sole goal was made by [[Hazem Mastouri]] on the 53rd minute, while it was [[Jan Paul van Hecke]] who sealed the Netherlands' top spot in the group stage.

Tunisia suffered its worst tournament performance to date, finishing without a single point despite winning matches in its previous two appearances in [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]] and [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022]]. This stood in stark contrast to [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification (CAF)#Group H|its qualifying campaign]], where it became the first African team to reach the World Cup without conceding a single goal.

==Discipline==
The team conduct ("fair play") score would have been used as a tiebreaker if the head-to-head and overall records of teams were tied. It would also be used as a tiebreaker for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-place teams|third-place ranking]] between groups if the overall records of teams were tied. The score was calculated based on yellow and red cards received by players and team officials in all group matches as follows:<ref name="regulations"/>
*yellow card: −1 point;
*indirect red card (second yellow card): −3 points;
*direct red card: −4 points;
*yellow card and direct red card: −5 points;

Only one of the above deductions could be applied to a player or team official in a single match.
